title: Two Keys, No Plaintext: stable evidence enters together

claims.summary: Sealed ingestion requires exactly two distinct envelopes and keys and rejects incomplete, duplicate, swapped, malformed, or reused sealed identities before preference derivation.

Both AES-256-GCM passes authenticate and validate packet, prompt, judge, metadata, plaintext, source, artifact, scorecard, and decision identities in memory before output is touched; no completed pass plaintext is written.

Only one A/B and one B/A reading from distinct fresh sessions can enter analysis, while ties, insufficient evidence, weak winners, missing defects, changed bytes, and side disagreement remain quarantined.
Stable qualified agreements become derived single-model Codex rows bound to both passes, four scorecards, packet and source identities, exact training bytes, minimum scores, margins, and defects.

The bridge is tested but the real B/A judgment, approved preferences, learned quality rows, adapter weights, held-out wins, device results, and paid-reference parity remain zero; public Scion stays base-only.
